summary: The chief priests and Pharisees ask Pilate to secure Jesus’ tomb, then seal the stone and post a guard to stop any claim that He has risen.
key_insight: Jesus’ enemies remembered what His friends seemed to have forgotten: “After three days I will rise.” Their seal and their guard, meant to prevent a hoax, became witnesses that no one stole the body.
story: On the next day, the day after the Preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees went together to Pilate.

“Sir,” they said, “we remember, while He was still alive, how that deceiver said, ‘After three days I will rise.’ Therefore command that the tomb be made secure until the third day, lest His disciples come by night and steal Him away, and say to the people, ‘He has risen from the dead.’ So the last deception will be worse than the first.”
Pilate said to them, “You have a guard; go your way, make it as secure as you know how.”
So they went and made the tomb secure, sealing the stone and setting the guard.

scene.label: On the Sabbath
scene.text: The Jewish day began at sunset, so whether these men came on Friday evening or Saturday morning, it was already the Sabbath. On Friday morning the chief priests had stayed outside Pilate’s headquarters to keep themselves ceremonially clean for the Passover (John 18:28). Now they went to the Gentile governor on a holy day to guard a grave.

scene.label: Whose guard?
scene.text: Pilate’s words can be read as “You have a guard,” meaning their own temple police, or as an order to take a guard of Roman soldiers. Later the guards report to the chief priests, who promise to protect them if the matter reaches the governor (Matthew 28:11–14). Many take that as a sign that they were Roman soldiers answerable to Pilate.

scene.label: The seal
scene.text: A cord was probably stretched across the stone and fixed with clay or wax bearing an official mark. A broken seal would show at once that someone had entered. Daniel’s den was sealed in the same way, “that the purpose concerning Daniel might not be changed” (Daniel 6:17).

scene.label: “That deceiver”
scene.text: The leaders had long said that Jesus led people astray; some in the crowds said, “He deceives the people” (John 7:12). To them, the first deception was His claim to be the Christ; the last would be a report that He had risen.

witnesses.matthew: Only Matthew tells of the guard, and he tells it in three parts: the sealing (27:62–66), the guards at the earthquake (28:2–4) and the bribe (28:11–15). He wrote while the story that the disciples stole the body was still “commonly reported among the Jews” (28:15), and he shows how it began.

seeing.reveals: Even Jesus’ enemies knew He had promised to rise. Nothing they did could stop Him; their precautions only made the evidence plainer.
seeing.living: Pilate told them, “make it as secure as you know how,” and they did their best. It counted for nothing against the purpose of God. When those with power seem to have sealed the outcome against Christ, remember the stone that Pilate’s seal could not hold in place.
seeing.ponder: Do you take Jesus’ promise to rise as seriously as His enemies did?

preaching.big_idea: Every effort to keep Jesus in the grave only made His resurrection harder to deny.
outline: A plan to keep the dead in place (64)
preaching.watch_for: The word “secure” comes three times in three verses (vv. 64, 65, 66). Matthew piles up human precautions so that the earthquake and the empty tomb in chapter 28 will stand out.

title: The Tomb Sealed and Guarded
